top_strength: Grant handled a long, messy self-reported inventory calmly and then converted it into a genuinely well-reasoned, right-sized estimate. He led pricing cleanly with "we charge $102 per hour per mover at the McKinney location and everything is included in that hourly rate, so the truck gas taxes, insurance, all the pads wrap and bands," nailed all four Clock bullets (on-site start, 2.5 hour minimum, 15-minute prorating, sense-check), and visibly adjusted the crew to the real scope rather than defaulting to the full-house build: "If you're just having us move the big furniture that you listed to me over the phone, I would feel fine sending you just a four man team on two trucks." The math checked out ($102 x 4 movers x 8 hours = $3,264) and he reassured on billing with "At the end of the day though you just pay for the time that we actually work."
coaching_note: Give the Save Your Ass prep speech - this call was the single best setup for it all week and Grant let it go by. The customer volunteered "I'm gonna, I'm gonna move as much loose stuff as I can this week and should be able to knock out a good portion of it," and Grant's entire response was "Gotcha." That was the moment to say prep before move day shortens the move and lowers the bill, then hand him the specific consolidation targets (kids' toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, photos off the walls, take a carload) - a customer already motivated to prep will act on every one of them, and on a projected 8-hour four-man job every hour saved is $408 off his bill. Secondary: the three differentiators (No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) were all skipped, which is 6 points and the reason a price-shopping customer walked away to "review it" instead of booking.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and steady but heavily transactional - "Gotcha," "Alrighty," and "Alrighty, good deal" repeat verbatim throughout with almost no acknowledgment of what the customer actually said, only three uses of Alex's name, no empathy markers, and an abrupt close that talked over the customer's last line.
